title: quest check --continuity --base <ref>: a base-relative record-continuity check so a dropped task record cannot pass a repository green (DEC-18)
description:
DEC-18 option A (operator answer relayed first-party via opum-agent, 2026-09-29; the decision record is DEC-18 on opum-agent records): put the tracker record-continuity check in quest itself rather than copying a script into 11 repositories.

MEASURED MOTIVATION (DEC-18 context, read at opum-agent dev): each of the fleet 11 Tracker integrity jobs runs only a list parse (quest task list --json) and a managed-block currency check, so a commit that DROPS a task record passes it green. Measured instance: ward-cli b2aad11 recorded WCLI-9 as a deletion because quest task complete moved the file and only the old path was staged; the job was green on it and on the next commit. Survey 2026-09-29T06:13Z: the gap is present in 11 of 11 repositories (26 workflow files read). A record may legitimately live in any of three directories: .quest/tasks, .quest/completed and .quest/archive.

WHAT TO BUILD: one base-relative continuity check in quest-cli (quest check --continuity --base <ref>, or similar): it fails when an id present at the merge base resolves nowhere after the change, covering all three directories including aliases.

SCOPE AND SEQUENCING: land on dev; cut NO release. It ships in the next lore and quest pair release (Article 3); after that each repository adds one workflow line and opum-cli-e2e qualifies it. QCLI-414, the held dev promotion, stays held.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest check --continuity --base <ref> exists (shape may differ if the CLI argues for it) and reads the task ids and aliases present at the merge base of <ref> and HEAD across .quest/tasks, .quest/completed and .quest/archive; it exits 0 when every one of them still resolves, and it reports how many it read and resolved, so a read of zero records is itself a failure rather than a silent pass.

Red side of the two-sided proof: with a record deliberately dropped between a base and the tip (its file gone from all three directories), the check exits non-zero and NAMES the dropped id in its output; measured on a real commit pair, not asserted.

Green side of the two-sided proof: a record legitimately relocated between .quest/tasks, .quest/completed and .quest/archive by complete, archive or demote between the base and the tip stays green with no false positive; measured across a real commit pair in this repository where such a relocation landed.
Aliases are covered: an id reachable at the base only through an alias still counts as resolved after a relocation, and an alias that stops resolving is reported by name.

plan: 1. Add mergeBase(a, b) to the git port and LocalGitPort, so the check reads ids at the true merge base of --base and HEAD rather than at the base ref tip (a branch behind its base must not be charged for ids it never had).

2. New application service src/application/checks/continuity.ts: list the task records present at that merge base across .quest/tasks, .quest/completed and .quest/archive/tasks, read each one, and resolve every id and alias it declares against the current store through the same case-folded id+alias key the CLI resolves references with. Fail closed on a base read of zero records and on an unreadable record. Drafts are deliberately out of scope: draft promote removes the draft record by design, so a draft id legitimately resolves nowhere afterwards and would be a guaranteed false positive.

3. Wire quest check --continuity --base <ref> through the manifest, help and dispatch. Broken continuity is drift on exit 6 naming every missing reference in `input`; an unresolvable --base ref is not_found, and a base with no records or an unreadable one is validation.

4. Tests: two-sided proof over real commits in temp workspaces (a deliberate drop goes red and names the id; complete, archive and demote relocations stay green), alias coverage both ways (a dotted alias still resolves after a relocation; a vanished alias is reported), and the zero-read refusal. Then the real-pair measurement runs against this repository own history.
5. Full suite under the pinned bun 1.4.2 PATH prefix; land via a PR to dev; cut NO release.
